Q: Problem installing TailwindCSS after `npx tailwindcss init` command - tailwindcss not recognized - npm error could not determine executable to run A:

For me, the process of installing with NPM failed; instead, I prefer that you create a Tailwind CSS binary using sources from GitHub and host it on your website.

Q: Visual Studio Code is showing only one file in the tab bar (can't open multiple files) A:

Check User interface / Tabs. You just need to add the following line in your settings.json file.

"workbench.editor.showTabs": false

I also think that How do I disable tabs in Visual Studio Code? is asking the exact opposite of what you are asking.

Q: Visual Studio Extension not running in VS2022 Experimental Instance A:

Had the same problem (with VS 2026) and I think it happened because the extension that I wanted to debug was also installed in my real Visual Studio.

  • When the experimental instance was created (here based on the VS 2026 instance "18.0_d788e3e3"), the installed extension was copied to a subdir of "C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Local\Microsoft\VisualStudio\18.0_d788e3e3Exp\Extensions\Extensions-18.0_d788e3e3" (a subdir with random name contained the extension files).
  • When building my extension, the files were copied to "C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Local\Microsoft\VisualStudio\18.0_d788e3e3Exp\Extensions\MyExtension\x.0.0.0".
  • After this, the message "error VSSDK1031: Extension ... could not be found" was printed and built aborted.

It started working after I increased the version number in "source.extension.vsixmanifest".

So the problem seems to happen if the version of the "to be debugged" extension project is the same as the version that was installed in the real Visual Studio instance when the experimental instance was created.

Recreating the experimental instance does not help as the version conflict happens again.

Q: How do I replace color: windowtext; A:

The old CSS2 system color names were deprecated many years ago. CSS Color Module Level 4 proposes to reintroduce a few, but most (including windowtext) would remain deprecated for a couple reasons:

These color keywords have been deprecated, however, as they are insufficient for their original purpose (making website elements look like their native OS counterparts), represent a security risk by making it easier for a webpage to “spoof” a native OS dialog, and increase fingerprinting surface, compromising user privacy.

Another relevant quote:

User agents must support these keywords, but should map them to "default" values, not based on the user’s OS settings (for example, mapping all the "background" colors to white and "foreground" colors to black). Authors must not use these keywords.

IMHO, you shouldn't try to recreate the authors' original intent nor rely on user agents' default support but define actual colors.

Q: How to avoid "zombie" Firebase anonymous users when linking Sign in with Apple? A:

What you call "zombie" users is effectively unavoidable as long as you have implemented a "continue as guest" mode that creates anonymous users. There is really nothing you can do to stop users from invoking this feature repeatedly, unless you have some way to assert the identity of a user so that they can do it only once (and if you had that, you might not have much use for Firebase Auth in the usual sense).

I suggest that you don't worry too much about this. Anonymous users don't cost you anything (for standard projects) and don't affect performance of Firebase Auth or your application.

If it bothers you to see these users in your system, or somehow they are causing problems or costs, you can write code on your backend to periodically purge them. You can also configure Firebase Auth to automatically delete them after 30 days if you've upgraded to Identity Platform. (This feature exists precisely for the reason you're explaining in your question.)

See:

  • How to bulk delete Firebase anonymous users

  • https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/ios/anonymous-auth#auto-cleanup
